predecessors.name: East Francia
predecessors.text: Saxony within East Francia: Old Saxony without the Aachen and Cologne circles, which belong to Lotharingia

successors.name: Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg
successors.text: the Land of Ratzeburg, the Land of Darzing and the Land of Hadeln, which the 1296 deed gave to Saxe-Lauenburg

successors.name: House of Ascania
successors.text: the Ascanian rump duchy: the lands of the later Saxe-Wittenberg and Saxe-Lauenburg, reading back from the 1296 partition

successors.name: Duchy of Westphalia
successors.text: the Westphalian lands around Arnsberg (Sauerland) given to the archbishop of Cologne

successors.name: Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg
successors.text: Henry the Lion's allodial lands around Brunswick

successors.name: Archbishopric of Magdeburg
successors.text: the city of Magdeburg, the bulk of the Magdeburg Börde, the Jerichow Land and the exclaves Halle, Oebisfelde and Jüterbog

successors.name: Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen
successors.text: the archbishopric with the city of Bremen

ledger.x: 911: Saxony enters the new German kingdom as a stem duchy.
936: Otto I makes Hermann Billung margrave over the Slavic tribes between the lower Elbe and the Baltic.
965: the Altmark passes to the new Northern March.
973: Hermann Billung dies at Quedlinburg and Otto II, newly emperor, makes Bernhard I the first Billung duke.
983: the Great Slav Rising ends the Billung March.
1106: the Billung dynasty ends and Lothar of Supplinburg becomes duke.
1138: Henry the Proud is stripped of Saxony and Albert the Bear is granted it.
1142: Henry the Lion becomes duke of Saxony.
1160: Niklot falls and Mecklenburg passes under the Saxon duke.
1167: Pribislav is restored in Mecklenburg as Henry the Lion's vassal.
1180: the Westphalian lands go to the archbishop of Cologne.
1180: Henry the Lion's overlordship over Mecklenburg ends with his deposition.
1180: the Bremen archbishopric's temporal land becomes imperial.
1180: the old stem duchy is broken up.
1180: the ducal title passes to the House of Ascania.
1295: the last year of the Ascanian Duchy of Saxony.

wars.name: Wendish Crusade
wars.outcome: The Saxon allies turned on the Obotrites; Niklot resisted the siege of Dobin but had to pay tribute.

wars.name: Henry the Lion's campaign against Niklot
wars.outcome: Denmark and Saxony allied in 1160; Niklot was killed at Burg Werle in August 1160 and the Obotrite territory was 'largely partitioned'.

wars.name: Welf-Ascanian struggle for Saxony
wars.outcome: Albert the Bear was granted Saxony in 1138 but renounced it in 1141; Henry the Lion was invested in 1142.

wars.name: League of nobles against Henry the Lion
wars.outcome: During Barbarossa's fourth Italian campaign a league of German nobles declared war on Henry; the war lasted until 1170.

wars.name: Fall of Henry the Lion
wars.outcome: Henry was isolated by the Hohenstaufen in 1176, tried in absentia in 1180, lost his titles and submitted at Erfurt in November 1181; the duchy was partitioned (Westphalia to Cologne).

certainty.note: Stem-duchy frontiers are approximate; the Elbe-Saale line to the Slavs and the Danish frontier on the Eider are not fixed by any treaty on the pages opened.
